checks.note: The rationale's plural 'Evaluations document repeated unsafe advice' rests on one study, e3. The e2 explanation cites 'the much smaller March total in the first claim's evidence', which is not in this case. Without it, e2 shows only scale, not growth after the forecast. The e1 explanation's 'increasing activity within user cohorts' is not in the quoted text. Calling the findings 'substantial support' leans past an unresolved outcome. Excerpt, conditions, dates and outcome are otherwise correct.

The excerpt is verbatim. The proposition is faithful. The rationale and limitations correctly say the base model was modified and that the source is reporting of developer interviews. The no-blame sentence matches Rianlan's quote. Dates, relation and outcome (supported, historical_observation) match.

The rationale and limitations are well supported and properly limited. The problem is e1's public excerpt, '30%'. The cited paragraph has two 30% figures, and the first, '30% of ChatGPT account holders, have little or no trust', is the opposite statistic. So the excerpt does not point to the supporting sentence. It should quote '30% of U.S. residents have a great deal or good amount of trust...'. e2, dates, period and outcome are correct.
